body:
The operator CLI `flask shoppinglist reset-password <email>` sets a new
password but leaves every existing auth token valid. change-password (T-45)
deliberately revokes all other sessions because a password change is the
standard response to a possibly-compromised account — the operator reset is
used in exactly the same situations (user lost the device / suspects
compromise / forgot password), so the same reasoning applies with more force:
after a reset, an attacker holding a stolen token keeps full access
indefinitely.

Fix: accounts.reset_password() should DELETE FROM auth_tokens WHERE
account_id = ? (all of them — there is no "current session" to spare in the
CLI case) in the same transaction as the hash update. Mention it in the CLI
help/README ("resets the password and signs out all devices").

Files: server/src/shoppinglist_server/accounts.py,
server/src/shoppinglist_server/cli.py (help text), server/tests/test_account.py,
server/README.md.
title: Server: operator reset-password leaves all existing sessions valid (inconsistent with T-45)
